<h2 id="toc-2">Does the presence of keywords/non-English characters in the URL affect SEO?</h2>
<p>John Mueller was asked this question on Twitter: "Would it have a bad SEO impact if French content web pages were used as URLs in English?" Here is his answer:</p>
<blockquote class="embed embed--twitter"><p>Twitter／X Post</p><a href="https://twitter.com/JohnMu/status/1296006310488662016" rel="noopener noreferrer">View original post on Twitter／X</a></blockquote>
<p>The general idea of the entire discussion thread is:</p>
<ol><li>When the content is indexed, whether there are keywords in the URL has minimal impact on SEO</li><li>Changing the URL is a site migration process for us, and it takes time to process, so don’t change it randomly if you have nothing to do.</li><li>The presence of non-English characters in the URL does not affect googlebot. You should decide what to use for the URL from the user's perspective.</li></ol>
<p class="has-dark-gray-color has-light-gray-background-color has-text-color has-background">I wrote an article<a href="./how-search-engines-crawl.html">How search engines crawl websites</a>’s article is very detailed but not short. If you don’t understand how the crawler works, you are welcome to come and fill in this aspect!</p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
<p></p>
</div></div>

<h2 id="toc-4">Several new features for Chrome</h2>
<p>The next version of Chrome has some nice features worth paying attention to:</p>
<p>1. <strong>Label the web page "Fast Page"</strong>- When long-pressing a link on a mobile phone, a "fast page" label will appear to inform the user of the user experience of the website. This label is based on<a href="./core-web-vitals-lcp-fid-cls.html">web vitals</a>comes from historical data.</p>
<div class="wp-block-image"><figure class="aligncenter size-large is-resized"><img alt="chrome marks web pages with good user experience" class="wp-image-1730" decoding="async" height="306" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2020/09/chrome-%E5%BF%AB%E9%80%9F%E9%A0%81%E9%9D%A2%E6%A8%99%E7%B1%A4.png" width="508"/><figcaption><a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2020/08/highlighting-great-user-experiences-on.html">Chrome will mark web pages with a good user experience as Fast Page</a></figcaption></figure></div>
<p><strong>2. Pagination classification and pagination preview</strong>- Tab Grouping can separate web pages in different colors and compress or expand them; while tab preview can run out a preview of the page when the mouse points to the tab.</p>
<figure class="wp-block-gallery columns-2 is-cropped"><ul class="blocks-gallery-grid"><li class="blocks-gallery-item"><figure><img alt="Illustration for SEO e-Newsletter Issue 15 – 2020.08.16~2020.08.31" class="wp-image-1733" data-id="1733" decoding="async" height="628" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2020/09/%E5%88%86%E9%A0%81%E5%88%86%E9%A1%9E.png" width="817"/></figure></li><li class="blocks-gallery-item"><figure><img alt="Illustration for SEO e-Newsletter Issue 15 – 2020.08.16~2020.08.31" class="wp-image-1734" data-id="1734" decoding="async" height="646" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2020/09/%E5%88%86%E9%A0%81%E9%A0%90%E8%A6%BD.png" width="919"/></figure></li></ul><figcaption class="blocks-gallery-caption"><a href="https://blog.google/products/chrome/organize-your-tabs-and-stay-productive-chrome/#jump-content:~:text=Group%20your%20tabs%2C%20then%20collapse%20them">Chrome’s new paging classification; folding/expanding; preview functions.</a></figcaption></figure>
<p><strong>3. Little Dinosaur QR Code Generator</strong>- Users can convert web pages into QR Codes with Chrome dinosaur patterns. It’s so cute. Below is the QR Code for this article🙃.</p>
<div class="wp-block-image"><figure class="aligncenter size-large is-resized"><img alt="chrome production QR Code" class="wp-image-1750" decoding="async" height="237" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Chrome%E6%81%90%E9%BE%8DQR-Code.png" width="237"/><figcaption>Scan and it will jump back here XD</figcaption></figure></div>

<h2 id="toc-5">[Template] Use Google Sheets to automatically record website web vitals</h2>
<p>Amit Agarwal shared this template, which can be connected to the PageSpeed Insights API through Apps Script to make the web page<a href="./core-web-vitals-lcp-fid-cls.html">User experience (web vitals)</a>scores are recorded daily on Google Sheets.</p>
<p>The entire setup is quite simple. It takes about 15 minutes to complete the setup by following the steps in the article.</p>

<h2 id="toc-6">AVIF image format that saves more space than WEBP</h2>
<p>AVIF is a new open source and free image format that can save 50% of JPEG images on average. It is considered to be more efficient than the WEBP format. Developers can choose lossy or lossless compression and can also support dynamic images.</p>
<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img alt="avif, webp, jpeg format comparison" class="wp-image-1736" decoding="async" height="268" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2020/09/AVIF%E5%9C%96%E7%89%87%E5%A3%93%E7%B8%AE-1024x268.png" width="1024"/><figcaption><a href="https://reachlightspeed.com/blog/using-the-new-high-performance-avif-image-format-on-the-web-today/">AVIF, WEBP, JPEG comparison chart (source)</a></figcaption></figure>

<h2 id="toc-7">Apple is rumored to launch its own search engine</h2>
<p>There are recent rumors that Apple may launch a search engine. Some signs are that they have opened a lot of related job openings, updated their applebot page, and many webmasters have recently seen that applebot has become quite active in the log file...etc. It's still a rumor stage, but if true, it will be a challenge to Google's search leadership position.</p>
<p>link:<a href="https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT204683">About applebot</a> / <a href="https://www.inside.com.tw/article/20829-apple-search-engine">Inside report (Chinese)</a></p>

<h2 id="toc-9">SEO Mythbusters: Site Migration</h2>
<p>This episode’s myth buster discusses Site Migration and has several good points: "<code>site move</code>Follow
What is the difference in Google's definition of<code>site migration</code>?", "What is the general process of Google's site migration", "Does the website need to use the URL change tool in GSC or can it be redirected directly with 301?"...etc.</p>
<p>I think it is quite interesting to use Martin’s dining truck/restaurant as an analogy: if the same dining cart moves from point A to point B, your evaluation of it will not change (site move); but if the restaurant changes its name, decoration and even price, you may need to visit it a few more times to decide whether it is worth recommending to friends (site migration).</p>

<h2 id="toc-10">Google Search Podcast EP.4 &amp; EP.5</h2>
<p>There are many good things in these two episodes of Search Off the Record. Some trivial topics are more interesting from the perspective of Googlers. I recommend friends who have time to listen to them.</p>
<p>The fourth episode includes the process of John, Gary, and Martin joining Google, how webmasters should treat comments on web pages...etc.</p>
<figure class="embed embed--spotify"><iframe allow="autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; fullscreen; picture-in-picture" loading="lazy" src="https://open.spotify.com/embed/episode/7lkxSrz3vlXV41YSwLCRUD" title="Spotify episode"></iframe><figcaption><a href="https://open.spotify.com/episode/7lkxSrz3vlXV41YSwLCRUD" rel="noopener noreferrer">View original content on Spotify</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>In the fifth episode, Martin discusses again<a href="./seo-newsletter-issue-12.html#toc-7">2 Wave Indexing Metaphor</a>, as well as honeymoon perios that are common in SEO (the traffic is very high when the webpage is released, but it will disappear after a few weeks), the origin of the sandbox, and crawl budget...etc.</p>
